I've read some differing views concerning the benefits and concerns with farm raised tilapia. First thing is you need lots and lots of fresh water. A fresh supply of fresh water that consistently refreshes the holding container for the fish is essential. Many people make the mistake of forgetting that the holding tank/pond is actually like an aquarium that has to be cleaned often and resupplied with new water. The consequence of not doing this is the fish will get polluted with parasites and toxins.

Commercially farmed fish has been hobbled by disease and hasn't been quite the panacea as it was originally marketed. It is not much different than privately farmed fish. Fish need a lot of space and a lot of water, otherwise all sorts of problems soon arise. I read a story some time ago, in which there was an attempt to use old quarry pits to raise farmed walleye. It didn't take long for the project coming to an end after finding out the fish were making the water toxic. It was a case of not enough space for the amount of fish and lack of a continuous flow of fresh water.

I personally won't eat farmed fish for the reasons above. Another issue is tilapia is already an invasive species in the United States. Texas, Florida, and California all list tilapia as an invasive species.
